what_its_for: Quinapril is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and heart failure. Lowering high blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It belongs to a group of medicines called ACE inhibitors, which help relax and widen your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard.
how_to_take: Take quinapril by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition and how your body responds. A common starting dose for high blood pressure is 10 mg once a day, which may be adjusted up to 80 mg per day. For heart failure, starting doses are usually lower (5 mg twice a day). Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store quinapril at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use this medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using salt substitutes or potassium supplements unless your doctor approves, as quinapril can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can increase the blood pressure-lowering effect and cause dizziness. Avoid over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve) without checking with your doctor first, as they can reduce how well quinapril works and harm your kidneys. Rise slowly from sitting or lying positions to avoid dizziness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this could be a serious reaction called angioedema); difficulty breathing or swallowing; severe dizziness or fainting; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat; signs of kidney problems such as decreased urination or swelling in your legs; a dry, persistent cough that bothers you (a common side effect that may require switching medicines); or if you become pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: You may start to notice your blood pressure improving within 1 to 2 hours after your first dose. However, it may take 2 to 4 weeks of regular use to get the full benefit of this medicine. Keep taking it every day even if you feel fine, because high blood pressure often has no symptoms.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take quinapril if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby, especially in the second and third trimesters. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding, as it is not known if quinapril passes into breast milk. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and may need a lower starting dose. Kidney disease: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose and monitor your kidney function more closely. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been established.
